# Answer: generator-shortcuts

## Strongest plausible rival

The strongest simple rival I found is **mirror the normalized template
horizontally whenever the color-1 marker lies to the left of the color-2 source;
otherwise copy it unchanged**. It fits all three canonical demonstrations. The
only canonical leftward move uses a horizontally symmetric template, so mirroring
and faithful copying are observationally identical there.

A second independent canonical-fitting shortcut is “copy only the first four
normalized template cells,” because every canonical source is a tetromino. The
proposed generator refutes both, but the exact witness below addresses the
mirror-on-left rival.

## How the output was checked

`repo/generators/54099d17f2dd/workspace/analyze_shortcuts.py` first checked the
rival against every canonical pair, then searched ordinary production draws. Its
independent oracle comes from `workspace/reference_probe.py`, which deliberately
does not import the generator's rule helpers. The probe executed the selected
canonical Racket program in batch and confirmed that the Racket output equals the
independent authority output above (`racket_matches_authority = true`). The full
source-bound record is `checks/shortcut-analysis.json`.

## Does the proposed generator emit such cases?

**Yes.** This is an ordinary non-override sample from the first production
profile, not a hand-constructed edge case. Every four-example cycle contains two
leftward asymmetric five-cell cases, so the mirror rival and the four-cell rival
are each refuted repeatedly; the 300-lesson census found both rivals refuted in
all 100 lessons per difficulty band and after all 1,500 query rotations.

Scope: this establishes separation from the declared plausible rivals, not from
every arbitrary feature-conditioned program.
